question: Which statement best describes Installable app?
options: A service worker is a script the browser can run separately from a page. It can intercept network requests and return cached files, but it does not automatically cache the whole app. It is like a helper stationed between a request and the network. Plan its lifecycle and update behavior carefully. For example, show an offline message when a user opens a route that was not cached. In practice, show an offline page when an uncached route cannot be reached.

A new service worker can wait while older pages remain open. Version caches and remove stale entries carefully. It is like replacing a tool while people are still using the old one. Test upgrades, failed downloads, and rollback so old caches do not trap users on broken files. For example, test a service worker update while a previous page remains open. In practice, test an update while an older tab remains open.

A cache strategy chooses whether a request uses the network, a saved response, or both. Use different rules for versioned assets, changing pages, and user data. It is like deciding which supplies to pack and how fresh they must be. Avoid serving private or stale data from an unsafe cache. For example, do not report a queued save as complete until the server confirms it. In practice, do not claim a queued change was saved before the server confirms it.

A web app manifest gives the browser a name, icons, colors, and launch behavior. On supported browsers, people may add the site to a home screen. It is like a label and launch card for the app. Installation support varies, so explain the experience without promising the same prompt on every device. For example, cache versioned scripts for reuse while fetching frequently changing account data from the network. In practice, cache a versioned app shell while fetching a user’s account data fresh.

Offline support should match a real user task. Explain which content is available and what must wait for a connection. Do not pretend a failed save succeeded. It is like marking a letter as sent only after it reaches the postbox. Queue actions only when conflicts and retries are handled. For example, remove old cache entries only after the new release can serve the needed files. In practice, remove obsolete cache entries without deleting assets still used by active pages.
